newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes stronger near 227 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes stronger near 227 per dollar.

text.p: Foreign currency supply strongly outweighed demand on Bulgaria's interbank market on Tuesday, boosting the lev to 226.50/227.60 per dollar at close from 229.80/230 in the morning, dealers said.
"Foreign currency demand was very low while supply surged and helped the lev to rebound by some 4-5 (levs) against the dollar in a single day," one dealer said.
The lev closed at 231.00/50 per dollar on Monday. @

Many banks and final clients tried to pare forex positions in favour of lev-denominated investments due to their high yield under the current main rate but there was almost no bidding for dollars, another dealer said.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) drastically raised its main rate to 25 percent monthly or 300 percent annually last week in a bid to restore confidence in local banks and support the weakening national currency.
The BNB was not seen buying dollars in the market which gave a further boost to the lev, traders said. @
Interbank trade was very thin as banks mostly covered end customers' purchase orders by their own funds, dealers said.
"There aren't many traders left in the market after the central bank put more banks under special supervision," a dealer said.

The BNB last week put another nine banks under special supevision in a second wave of bank restructuring aimed at stabilising the country's crumbling banking sector in line with pledges made to multilateral lenders.
The central bank filed insolvency procedures through the courts against five banks in May and June. @ -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
